tracker.research_notes: Seeded 2026-09-30 from Claude's general knowledge; not verified.

triage.why: Tax/finance software giant; QA/SDET roles plausible in regulated fintech, but domain not listed interest.

remote_policy.summary: Hybrid model: teams are expected onsite three days per week, combining in-person collaboration with virtual flexibility; some tax expert roles are described as working remotely.

signals.summary: Restructuring cuts about 3,000 jobs, roughly 17% of the workforce, to reduce complexity and accelerate AI focus.
Intuit stock fell nearly 5% in morning trading on the day the layoff restructuring was reported.

fit.rationale: Intuit builds tax, accounting and fintech platforms (TurboTax, QuickBooks), a regulated, compliance-heavy domain that suits the candidate's V&V rigor. But it is hybrid with three onsite days weekly, Maine eligibility varies, 17% of staff were just cut, and no QA

research.approach_role: Chief Data Officer (only named leader; no QA leader in facts)
research.outreach_angle: Fifteen years of C#/.NET test automation and FDA-regulated V&V maps to Intuit's compliance-heavy tax and fintech platforms, though I would need a Maine-eligible remote or flex arrangement.
research.red_flags: Hybrid three days onsite, Maine eligibility uncertain; 3,000-job (17%) restructuring; no QA openings listed; finance/tax domain not among stated interests.
research.notes: Intuit: 5k+ employees, tax/finance software. Remote policy is hybrid, three onsite days per week, some tax-expert roles remote; Maine eligibility marked varies, so confirm residency terms early. Stability dented by a ~3,000-role (17%) restructuring tied to AI focus plus a ~5% stock dip. No QA postings found; only named leader is a Chief Data Officer.
